newsitem.title: CANADA: GasAndes pipeline delayed after court injunction.
newsitem.headline: GasAndes pipeline delayed after court injunction.

text.p: Work on the Argentina-Chile GasAndes natural gas pipeline has been delayed after a Chilean court ordered an injunction pending new studies on mud and rockslide prevention at one section, a spokesman with the project's lead company said on Monday.

"We're in a waiting mode right now. It was just late last week that the court had ordered these technical studies. So that will take a week or so for those studies to come in and then we'll hear from there," Jeff Flood, spokesman for Calgary-based NOVA Corp, said.
The official opening for the $325 million project, led by NOVA and Chilgener SA, was set for August 7.
Flood said work on the pipeline was about 98 percent complete, but the consortium was not allowed to perform flow tests on the pipeline between San Alfonso, Chile and Santiago under the injunction.
GasAndes had made a commitment to the town of San Alfonso to build diversion structures that would protect the pipeline's right-of-way in the event of a rock or mudslide.
But work on the diversion structures was pushed back after an unusually wet May, Flood said.

The consortium believed gas could safely flow before the structures were completed in Mid-August, but some San Alfonso residents disagreed and last week won the injunction from the appeal court of San Miguel preventing gas flowing through the community, he said.
Flood said GasAndes appealed the injunction.
Also, the court ordered technical studies on such factors as rainfall, the potential for rockslides and safety of the pipeline systems.
"They are waiting for those reports over the next week or so and based on those reports they will have the option of lifting the injunction or leaving it in place," he said.
Testing on the pipeline sections upstream from San Alfonso had continued with the use of shut-off valves, he said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
